instruction:
You are working in the container at /dayjs, a checkout of the dayjs JS library. Your job is READ-ONLY investigation of the repository's git state. Do NOT modify any file.

Run and report the full output of:
- `cd /dayjs && git status --porcelain=v1 && git log --oneline -40`
- `cd /dayjs && git log --stat -5`
- `cd /dayjs && git diff HEAD --stat && git diff HEAD`
- `cd /dayjs && git log --oneline -20 -- src/plugin/timezone/index.js`
- `cd /dayjs && git log -p -3 -- src/plugin/timezone/index.js | head -200`
- `cd /dayjs && head -40 CHANGELOG.md`
- `cd /dayjs && git tag | tail -20`

Report verbatim the relevant outputs, especially anything showing whether the working tree is dirty, whether recent commits touched src/plugin/timezone/index.js, and what the CHANGELOG says at the top. Do not change anything.

You are working in the container at /dayjs, a checkout of the dayjs JS library. Your job is READ-ONLY investigation: establish the baseline test status. Do NOT modify any file in /dayjs (no edits, no new files inside /dayjs).

Steps:
1. `cd /dayjs && node -v && npx jest --version`
2. Run the full test suite: `cd /dayjs && npx jest --coverage=false 2>&1 | tail -80` (this may take a few minutes; use a generous timeout, e.g. 600000 ms).
3. Also run: `cd /dayjs && TZ=Pacific/Auckland npx jest test/timezone.test --coverage=false 2>&1 | tail -40` and `cd /dayjs && TZ=America/New_York npx jest test/plugin/timezone.test --coverage=false 2>&1 | tail -60`.
4. Report: node version, the exact list of FAILING test names (full names) from each run, the pass/fail counts, and any error messages/stack traces. Be precise and complete. Do not attempt any fixes.

You are working in the container at /dayjs, a checkout of the dayjs JS library. Your job is READ-ONLY: inspect source files and report facts. Do NOT modify anything.

Report the full contents (with line numbers) of these files:
- /dayjs/src/plugin/timezone/index.js
- /dayjs/src/plugin/utc/index.js
- /dayjs/src/utils.js
- /dayjs/src/constant.js
- /dayjs/types/plugin/timezone.d.ts
- /dayjs/test/plugin/utc.test.js
- /dayjs/test/plugin/utc-utcOffset.test.js
- /dayjs/test/parse.test.js

Also run and report: `cd /dayjs && grep -rn "tz" docs/en/Plugin.md | head -60` and `cd /dayjs && sed -n '1,80p' docs/en/Plugin.md` and `cd /dayjs && grep -rn -i "timezone" README.md docs/en/*.md | head -40`.

Finally, report any place in the repository (docs, types, comments) that documents the expected behaviour of `dayjs.tz(...)` (what it accepts: string, timestamp, Date, Dayjs object) and of the `Z`/`ZZ` format tokens. Quote the exact lines.

You are working in the container at /dayjs, a checkout of the dayjs JS library. Your job is READ-ONLY investigation: figure out how the timezone plugin's `dayjs.tz()` handles non-string inputs and how `format('Z')` is computed, by reading code and running small experiments. Do NOT modify any file in /dayjs except that you may create ONE temporary file /tmp/probe2.mjs or /tmp/probe2.js and run it with node using dynamic import of the built files if possible; delete it when done. Prefer reading source over running code.

Concretely:
1. Read /dayjs/src/index.js (full), /dayjs/src/plugin/utc/index.js, /dayjs/src/plugin/timezone/index.js, /dayjs/src/utils.js and report how `valueOf()`, `utcOffset()`, `format('Z')` and `toDate()` behave for an instance created by `dayjs.tz(input, timezone)`.
2. Trace by hand (and verify by running node if feasible) what `dayjs.tz(1401638400000, 'America/New_York')`, `dayjs.tz(new Date(1401638400000), 'America/New_York')` and `dayjs.tz(dayjs(1401638400000), 'America/New_York')` return with the CURRENT code, and what moment-timezone returns for the same inputs. Note that the current code does `d.utc(input).valueOf()` for all inputs.
3. Report exactly which inputs produce wrong results and the numeric/string values observed.

Report findings as a concise list of facts with the commands you ran and their raw output. Do not edit source files.

You are working in the container at /dayjs, a checkout of the dayjs JS library. Your job is to empirically probe the behaviour of the timezone plugin so we can identify bugs. You may create ONE temporary scratch script at /dayjs/probe.js and run it; you MUST delete /dayjs/probe.js when done. Do NOT modify any other file in /dayjs.

Create /dayjs/probe.js containing roughly:

```js
import dayjs from './src'
import utc from './src/plugin/utc'
import timezone from './src/plugin/timezone'
import moment from 'moment-timezone'

dayjs.extend(utc)
dayjs.extend(timezone)
const NY = 'America/New_York'
const LA = 'America/Los_Angeles'
const ts = 1401638400000 // 2014-06-01T12:00:00Z

const show = (label, a, b) => console.log(label, '|', a, '|', b, '|', a === b ? 'OK' : 'DIFF')

// parse timestamp / Date / Dayjs object
show('tz(ts)', dayjs.tz(ts, NY).format(), moment.tz(ts, NY).format())
show('tz(ts).valueOf', dayjs.tz(ts, NY).valueOf(), moment.tz(ts, NY).valueOf())
show('tz(Date)', dayjs.tz(new Date(ts), NY).format(), moment.tz(new Date(ts), NY).format())
show('tz(Dayjs)', dayjs.tz(dayjs(ts), NY).format(), moment.tz(moment(ts), NY).format())
show('tz(dayjs.utc)', dayjs.tz(dayjs.utc(ts), NY).format(), moment.tz(moment.utc(ts), NY).format())

// format Z
show('format Z (convert)', dayjs('2014-06-01T12:00:00Z').tz(LA).format('Z'), moment('2014-06-01T12:00:00Z').tz(LA).format('Z'))
show('format Z (parse)', dayjs.tz('2014-06-01 12:00', NY).format('Z'), moment.tz('2014-06-01 12:00', NY).format('Z'))
show('format Z (parse ts)', dayjs.tz(ts, NY).format('Z'), moment.tz(ts, NY).format('Z'))
show('format Z (parse Date)', dayjs.tz(new Date(ts), NY).format('Z'), moment.tz(new Date(ts), NY).format('Z'))
show('format Z (parse Dayjs)', dayjs.tz(dayjs(ts), NY).format('Z'), moment.tz(moment(ts), NY).format('Z'))
show('format ZZ', dayjs('2014-06-01T12:00:00Z').tz(LA).format('ZZ'), moment('2014-06-01T12:00:00Z').tz(LA).format('ZZ'))
show('format full', dayjs('2014-06-01T12:00:00Z').tz(LA).format(), moment('2014-06-01T12:00:00Z').tz(LA).format())
show('utcOffset', dayjs('2014-06-01T12:00:00Z').tz(LA).utcOffset(), moment('2014-06-01T12:00:00Z').tz(LA).utcOffset())
show('tz(ts) offset', dayjs.tz(ts, NY).utcOffset(), moment.tz(ts, NY).utcOffset())
show('tz(ts) format Z', dayjs.tz(ts, NY).format('Z'), moment.tz(ts, NY).format('Z'))
show('guess type', typeof dayjs.tz.guess(), typeof moment.tz.guess())
show('tz(ts) tz(LA)', dayjs.tz(ts, NY).tz(LA).format(), moment.tz(ts, NY).tz(LA).format())
```

Run it with: `cd /dayjs && npx babel-node probe.js` (if babel-node is unavailable, try `cd /dayjs && node -r @babel/register probe.js`, or `cd /dayjs && npx jest --roots probe ...` variants; report what worked). Also run it under a couple of TZ env values, e.g. `TZ=UTC`, `TZ=America/New_York`, `TZ=Pacific/Auckland`, since behaviour may depend on the local zone.

Then DELETE /dayjs/probe.js (`rm /dayjs/probe.js`) and confirm with `ls /dayjs` that it is gone.

Report: the exact command used, the full console output for each TZ, and which comparisons DIFF. Do not attempt to fix any source file.

In /dayjs (dayjs JS library). Fix a bug in src/plugin/timezone/index.js in `proto.tz`: `const diff = (this.toDate() - new Date(target)) / 1000 / 60` is fractional when the instance has non-zero milliseconds (toLocaleString drops ms), so `d(target).utcOffset(localUtcOffset - diff, true)` gets a fractional offset and `format('Z')`/`format()` produce garbage like '-07:0.123'. Fix: round the diff, i.e. `const diff = Math.round((this.toDate() - new Date(target)) / 1000 / 60)`. Keep everything else identical. Verify: (a) `cd /dayjs && npx jest test/plugin/timezone.test.js --coverage=false` fully passes; (b) with a temporary script /tmp/check4.js run as `cd /dayjs && BABEL_ENV=test npx babel-node /tmp/check4.js` (requires /dayjs/src, plugin/utc, plugin/timezone, moment-timezone) assert that dayjs('2014-06-01T12:00:00.123Z').tz('America/Los_Angeles').format('Z') === '-07:00' and equals moment's, and that dayjs('2014-06-01T12:00:00.123Z').tz('America/Los_Angeles').format() equals moment's; delete the temp script. Do not modify other files or tests. Report the diff and verification output.

In /dayjs (dayjs JS library). Bug in src/plugin/duration/index.js (hidden test name: 'Creating milliseconds'). Read the whole file and find why creating a duration from milliseconds is wrong, e.g. compare with moment: `cd /dayjs && node -e "const m=require('moment');const d=m.duration(100);console.log(d.asMilliseconds(),d.milliseconds())"` and with dayjs via a temp script /tmp/check18.js run as `cd /dayjs && BABEL_ENV=test npx babel-node /tmp/check18.js` requiring /dayjs/src and /dayjs/src/plugin/duration, printing dayjs.duration(100).asMilliseconds(), .milliseconds(), .asSeconds(), dayjs.duration({ milliseconds: 100 }).asMilliseconds(), dayjs.duration(1, 'ms')... Compare each against moment.duration equivalents and find the divergence (suspect the MILLISECONDS constant / unit mapping in the duration plugin). Fix the source minimally so dayjs.duration(...) matches moment for milliseconds, then verify: (a) `cd /dayjs && npx jest test/plugin/duration.test.js --coverage=false` fully passes (report any pre-existing failures separately, do not edit tests); (b) the temp script output matches moment for the ms cases. Delete the temp script. Do not modify tests or other files. Report the exact diff and all outputs.

In /dayjs (dayjs JS library). Bug in src/plugin/weekYear/index.js: `proto.weekYear` only handles the case `weekOfYear === 1 && month === 11` (returning year+1) and misses the symmetric case where a January date belongs to the last week of the previous week-year; it must return year - 1 when `month === 0 && weekOfYear >= 52`. The hidden test is named 'yearStart: 4' (a locale with `yearStart: 4`, e.g. check /dayjs/src/locale/*.js for locales defining yearStart, and /dayjs/node_modules/moment/locale for the matching moment locale). Implement: in `proto.weekYear`, after the existing `if (weekOfYear === 1 && month === 11) return year + 1`, add `if (month === 0 && weekOfYear >= 52) return year - 1`. Verify: (a) `cd /dayjs && npx jest test/plugin/weekYear.test.js test/plugin/advancedFormat.test.js test/plugin/weekOfYear.test.js --coverage=false` all pass; (b) with a temp script /tmp/check11.js run as `cd /dayjs && BABEL_ENV=test npx babel-node /tmp/check11.js` (require /dayjs/src, plugin/weekYear, plugin/weekOfYear, the locale with yearStart: 4, and moment with the matching locale) compare dayjs(d).weekYear() with moment(d).weekYear() for a range of dates around new year (e.g. 2018-12-25..2019-01-10) with that locale set, both for dayjs and moment. Delete the temp script. Do not modify tests or other files. Report the diff and the comparison output.

In /dayjs (dayjs JS library). Bug in src/plugin/customParseFormat/index.js: the `A`/`a` (meridiem) tokens only match the literal English 'AM'/'PM' via `matchUpperCaseAMPM = /[AP]M/` and `matchLowerCaseAMPM = /[ap]m/`, so locale meridiems (e.g. zh-cn '上午'/'下午') cannot be parsed. Hidden tests: 'meridiem locale AM' and 'meridiem locale PM', expected behaviour e.g. `dayjs('2018-05-02 上午 1:02:03', 'YYYY-MM-DD A h:mm:ss', 'zh-cn').format('YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss') === '2018-05-02 01:02:03'` and with '下午' === '2018-05-02 13:02:03' (check src/locale/zh-cn.js for its `meridiem` function). Implement: use `matchWord` (= /\d*[^\s\d-:/()]+/) as the regex for the A and a tokens, and set `this.afternoon` via a helper that consults the current `locale.meridiem` when present, e.g. iterate hours 1..24 and compare `meridiem(hour, 0, isLowerCase)` with the input, setting isAfternoon when the matched hour is >= 12; when the locale has no `meridiem`, keep the old behaviour (`input === 'PM'` for A, `'pm'` for a). Make sure the existing English behaviour is unchanged. Verify: (a) `cd /dayjs && npx jest test/plugin/customParseFormat.test.js --coverage=false` fully passes; (b) temp script /tmp/check15.js run as `cd /dayjs && BABEL_ENV=test npx babel-node /tmp/check15.js` asserting the two zh-cn cases above (require /dayjs/src, plugin/customParseFormat, locale/zh-cn); delete it afterwards. Do not modify tests or other files. Report the exact diff and outputs.

In /dayjs (dayjs JS library, node 10, jest). Fix a bug in src/plugin/timezone/index.js: `d.tz(input, timezone)` currently does `const localTs = d.utc(input).valueOf()` for ALL inputs, which treats numbers, js Date objects and Dayjs objects as wall-clock strings, shifting the result by the zone offset. Required behaviour: for non-string input, the input is an absolute instant, so `dayjs.tz(1401638400000, 'America/New_York')` must equal `moment.tz(1401638400000, 'America/New_York')` (i.e. same as `dayjs(1401638400000).tz('America/New_York')`), and same for `new Date(ts)` and `dayjs(ts)`. Fix by adding, right after `const previousOffset = tzOffset(+d(), timezone)` in `d.tz`, a guard: `if (typeof input !== 'string') { return d(input).tz(timezone) }` (keep the string path unchanged). Then verify: (a) `cd /dayjs && npx jest test/plugin/timezone.test.js --coverage=false` still fully passes; (b) write a temporary script /tmp/check1.js run with `cd /dayjs && BABEL_ENV=test npx babel-node /tmp/check1.js` that requires /dayjs/src, /dayjs/src/plugin/utc, /dayjs/src/plugin/timezone and moment-timezone, and asserts dayjs.tz(1401638400000,'America/New_York').format() === moment.tz(1401638400000,'America/New_York').format(), same for new Date(ts) and dayjs(ts), and that valueOf() matches moment; delete /tmp/check1.js afterwards. Do not modify any other file, do not modify tests. Report the exact diff you applied and the verification output.

In /dayjs (dayjs JS library). Bug in src/locale/nl.js: the Dutch locale's `ordinal` is `n => `${n}.``, which makes `dayjs(...).locale('nl').format('Do')` disagree with moment's Dutch locale (test name: 'Format Day of Month Do 1 - 31'). Determine the correct Dutch ordinal by reading /dayjs/node_modules/moment/locale/nl.js (look at its `ordinal` function) and by running moment: `cd /dayjs && node -e "const m=require('moment');require('moment/locale/nl');m.locale('nl');console.log([1,2,3,4,11,12,13,21,22,23,31].map(d=>m('2018-05-'+String(d).padStart(2,'0')).format('Do')).join(' '))"`. Then change ONLY the `ordinal` line in src/locale/nl.js so that dayjs matches moment for days 1..31 (verify with a temp script /tmp/check8.js run as `cd /dayjs && BABEL_ENV=test npx babel-node /tmp/check8.js` requiring /dayjs/src, /dayjs/src/plugin/advancedFormat, /dayjs/src/locale/nl and moment: for every day 1..31 of 2018-05, compare dayjs(...).locale('nl').format('Do') with moment(...).locale('nl').format('Do')). Delete the temp script. Also run `cd /dayjs && npx jest test/plugin/advancedFormat.test.js test/locale --coverage=false` and report results. Do not modify tests or other files. Report the exact diff and outputs.
